# Review — secret-history-267-270 (§§267–270)

## Pass 1

Scope: conventions.md, runbook.md, packet.md, units.json, known-forms.json, novel-forms.json and the published
model only. Edits were made to units.json in place by script. `t` is untouched (511 words, contiguous, `ln` / `p`
and key order unchanged). Checked by script: every `t` word equals the packet word; every first-morph Ming
bracket equals the packet's Ming gloss; quote marks in `l` mirror `t`, those in `i` are balanced.
Totals (grouped): 0 critical, 2 major, 9 moderate, 20 minor.

### Major

1. **U42 · i, n · major.** `i` set "the Baqtad people, with Sultan Qaliba" as two items, contradicting its own `l`
   ("Baγtad people's Qaliba Sultan-to"): `Baγtad irgen-ü` is a genitive, so Qaliba is the Sultan *of the Baqtad
   people*. Now: "as for the people his own father Chinggis Qahan had left unfinished — Sultan Qaliba of the Baqtad
   people, against whom there had been a campaign —". Note states the parse.
2. **U43 · l, i, n, morph Čormaqan gloss · major.** "Chormaqan" against the house name Sormaqan (260-264). Changed to
   Sormaqan in `l`, `i` and the gloss ("Sormaqan (printed Čormaqan)"); the note no longer says the two are "kept apart".

### Moderate

3. **U6 · l, n, morph dura and bulγaba · moderate.** (Drafter's bulγaba doubt.) `l` "heart-evil" put the Ming
   gloss 惡 into the Mongol line; now "heart upset(?)". The Ming gives 惡 (on dura) + 心了, which is a different Ming
   gloss from the glossary's bulγa- "to fight" (厮殺), so the Ming-led "revulsion" in `i` stands, but the gloss and
   note now say it is taken from the Ming and tentative, and set it against the glossary sense.
4. **U8 · n, morph -fkün · moderate.** Note and gloss called the f "probably a slip for -kün". The Han is 惕坤 (t +
   kün), so f is a slip for t: ending -tkün, taken as one ending like -dkün/-dqun (house, 265-266), sense from the
   Ming 者. Suffix lemma changed to `-tkün`.
5. **U20 · i, n · moderate.** `i` lost the frame eke ečige-ji … kürtele ("from mothers and fathers down to the
   offspring of the offspring") and translated the Ming-unglossed muquli musquli as "a trace (?)". House practice
   leaves unglossed words untranslated (torluγ / torulmiši, 189-190). Now: "from the Tangut people's mothers and
   fathers down to the offspring of their offspring, leaving no muquli musquli of them"; note matched.
6. **U29, U53 · i · moderate.** "commanders" for nojad; house (224-226) is noyan → "officer". Now "officers".
7. **U30 · i · moderate.** "Ködö'e-Aral" is remembered English, not derivable from Ködeġü (Han 闊迭兀). Rule-built
   "Köde'ü-Aral" (as Žeġü- → Je'ü- in house names). Same in `about`.
8. **U48, U50, U69 (l, i), U48 n, morph glosses, about · moderate.** "Güyük" is remembered English for printed
   Güjüg; the ž → j rule gives "Güjüg". Changed everywhere. Han 古余克 suggests the sound Güyük, so this is for the
   owner (see Remaining doubts).
9. **about · moderate.** "Two years on" is wrong on the text's own data (Pig year → Rat year is the next year) and
   rests on outside chronology: now "In the Rat year". "West" is not in the Mongol: removed. "the Adil and Jajaq" read
   Adil-Jajaq as two rivers; the text has one name glossed 河名: now "the Adil-Jajaq river". "Güyük" → Güjüg.
10. **U59 · l, n; U60 · l · moderate.** The unit's last word, Sübeġetei-jin, was missing from U59's `l` and wrongly
    carried by U60's `l` (whose `t` lacks it). `l` now follows `t`; the note in U59 says the word belongs in sense
    with gežige in U60, whose `i` carries it. (The cut itself is not moved: `t` is fixed.)
11. **U65 · i, n · moderate.** (Drafter's irežüġüi doubt.) "So saying, he came." follows a closing mark and reads as
    Ögödei. Subject decided as Cha'adai (it answers ügüležü irerün at the head of his speech): `i` now "So saying,
    Cha'adai came." Note records that Shiratori's closing mark falls before keġežü irežüġüi and that it is not clear
    whether it closes all of Ögödei's speech.

### Minor

12. U0 · i · Časutu → Chasutu (house, 265-266). U0 · n · the finite verb irebe is two units on, not "the next unit's sentence".
13. U4 · morph jesüd ×4 · lemma `jesü-` (a verb-stem shape) → `jesün`, as miṅγad < miṅγan; gloss reworded.
14. U7 · morph γutaγ̇ar · lemma follows the glossary: `γutaγar`.
15. U8 · n · closing quotation is in the next unit, not "the unit after next".
16. Four -že morphs (U14 bi-že, U16 abuγ̇ai-že, U58 bolžuγ̇u-že, U69 bi-že) · "indeed, so be it" → "assertion particle: indeed, surely" (glossary; "so be it" suggests an optative).
17. U24 · n · Ming 絕着 → 窮絕 (packet). U27 · n · 項每 is not under this word here (Ming 等). U31 · n · 提名來的 → 名了的.
    U35 · n · 貼身 → 親近. U40 · n · 了着 → 了了着. U61 · n · 寬廣 → 廣盛. U67 · n · 敎出去咱 → 敎出咱. U59 · n · 來的 → 來. (Ming glosses quoted from the glossary instead of this packet.)
18. U33 · n · "next five units" → four. U35 · n · "men" in `i` acknowledged as supplied.
19. U38 · i · mün had become "too" and josu "proper": now "by that very rule" (as U55 "by the same rule").
20. U44, U47 · i · "Sübegetei the hero" → "Sübegetei-Ba'atur" (house, 230-236).
21. U49 · l · closing `"` after aqalatuγai restored (l mirrors Shiratori's marks).
22. U51, U52 · i · ulus (Ming 百姓) "realm" → "people", as elsewhere in the part; "the eldest son" → "their own eldest sons". U51 · n · locator "unit 414–421" clarified.
23. All `l`, `i`, titleEn, part, about · curly apostrophes (Cha’adai, Arbuqa’s) → straight, as in the model and the house names; curly quotation marks kept.

## Findings refused, and why

- **muγ̇ud** (U4). Kept "boys": Ming 兒(每) fixes the sense; the Han 訥 doubt is already in the note and the gloss. No alternative reading can be got from the packet.
- **Buqar / Kerel as peoples** (U45). Kept: the Ming here is 種名 for both, which outranks the glossary's "town" / "quarrel" (Ming 城名 / 鬪 at other places); gloss and note already say so.
- **büteġüj-e "in the dark"** (U5). Kept: follows the Ming 暗行; note already gives "closed" as the alternative.
- **Nested speech 267** (U8–U9). Kept the drafter's reading (Chinggis named in third person inside the quoted decree is Shiratori's marking, not a fault in `i`); the double keġen is rendered once each.
- **kürkü-jin lemma kür-** (glossary says kürü-). Kept kür-: the glossary itself uses kür- for kürtele.
- **qorčin as one lemma** (glossary qor-či-n). Kept: house 260-264 uses qorči/qorčin.
- **ketülün "-ün" vs glossary "-n".** Kept: both valid analyses of the same form.
- **Moving the U59/U60 cut.** Refused: `t` must be preserved; fixed in `l`, `n`.
- **titleEn "western campaigns".** Left: editorial naming; only the `about` assertion was fixed.
- **U58 "And this custom too".** Kept: renders Ene ba.
- **Adding a muquli ~ muqudγa- link.** Refused: speculation.

## Remaining doubts

- U8-U9: whether the first quotation (62–78) really contains "Chinggis Qahan said there" in the third person, and what iregdežü with Šidurqu-ji means.
- U15: "Having come to hear a companion's poisonous words" (üge-dür irežü) is loose; whose speech is not said.
- U35: Qān ečige-jin followed by min-u: "Father Qan's men … my side" is a guess at who speaks.
- U42-U44: the accusatives (Baγtad, Sübeġetei baγ̇atur-i) wait for verbs the Mongol does not give; "sent out" is supplied.
- U65: where Ögödei's first speech ends (Shiratori's mark vs the sense).
- Güjüg vs Güyük, and Sormaqan vs Shiratori's Čormaqan: owner's call.
- muquli musquli; olulčan; ečidgen; berkeldü-; -dqun/-tkün as one ending remain tentative.
